jobs.title: Sr. Data Analyst
jobs.description:
Company Description:

Sagetap is a rapidly growing startup changing how enterprise technology executives discover and evaluate software. Our AI-driven platform anonymously connects tech buyers with the industry’s most credible technology vendors, helping them cut through the noise and solve their biggest problems.

Backed by investors like NFX Ventures, Uncorrelated Ventures, and Emergent Ventures, we are on a mission to fundamentally change software discovery for senior technology leaders, fostering meaningful connections in a non-sales setting.

We’re a tight-knit, fast-moving team that values curiosity, transparency, and impact. If you’re energetic, results-oriented, and excited to work in an early-stage environment, come help us shape the future of technology buying at Sagetap!
Job Description

As a Senior Data Analyst at Sagetap, you'll serve as the strategic analytics partner to Product, Growth, Engineering, Design, and Leadership. You'll use data to shape product strategy, influence roadmap decisions, and identify the highest-impact opportunities for marketplace growth.

You'll own the product analytics function; from defining KPIs and experimentation frameworks to building trusted reporting and scalable datasets. Your work will help leadership understand what is happening in the business, why it is happening, and what we should do next.

What you will do:

Serve as the strategic analytics partner to Product, Growth, Engineering, and Design, helping prioritize roadmap investments through quantitative analysis and marketplace insights.
Support growth by generating insights and reports from Sagetap proprietary data.
Own the measurement framework for product initiatives by defining KPIs, evaluating feature performance, identifying root causes behind metric movement, and presenting recommendations to leadership.
Lead experimentation strategy by designing, evaluating, and scaling A/B tests and product experiments.
Build executive-ready dashboards, analyses, and self-service reporting that improve decision making across Product, GTM, and Leadership.
Create and maintain scalable analytics datasets using DBT and modern data modeling best practices.
Manage Database Categorization of our technology categories and vendors.
Partner with executive leadership to answer strategic business questions and influence company priorities through data.
Support growth by generating insights and reports from Sagetap proprietary data. 
Research cybersecurity and AI markets to identify trends that inform product strategy.
Leverage LLMs to improve internal workflows and enrich Sagetap's product database.

Qualifications:

5+ years of experience in Product Analytics, Data Analytics, Growth Analytics, or Data Science, preferably in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, or product-led growth companies.
Expert SQL and Python proficiency.
Hands-on experience with DBT, Mixpanel, Omni (or similar BI tools), Git, experimentation frameworks, and modern data warehouses.
Experience defining KPIs and measurement strategies for product organizations.
Strong business judgment and ability to translate complex analyses into clear executive recommendations.
Experience influencing cross-functional teams and partnering with senior stakeholders.
Highly organized, proactive, AI-forward, and comfortable thriving in ambiguity.

What we are looking for: 

Strategic thinker who connects data to business outcomes.
Ownership mentality with the ability to independently drive high-impact initiatives.
Excellent communication and storytelling skills.
Curiosity, experimentation mindset, and bias toward action.
Experience mentoring analysts or establishing analytics best practices is a plus.

Additional Information

Location: Remote or Hybrid in San Francisco

Tools: DBT, Mixpanel, Omni, Hex, Hightouch 

Environment:
High accountability, strong ownership, and thoughtful flexibility

What you will have at Sagetap:

Early-stage equity
Competitive salary + 401(k) 
Comprehensive healthcare benefits
Real ownership in building a category-defining product
Opportunity to work closely with a high-performing, mission-driven team

Diversity drives innovation, enables better decisions to support our customers, and inspires change for the better. We’re building a culture where differences are valued and welcomed. We work together to bring out the best in each other. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or any other applicable legally protected characteristics in the location in which the candidate is applying.

jobs.title: Supply Chain Data Analyst
jobs.description:
*Please note that we do not accept unsolicited candidate introductions, referrals, or resumes from external recruiters or staffing agencies.

Supply Chain Data Analyst

Location: Candidates must be located in the PST or MST time zones.

Background Check Requirement

As part of our hiring process, Frontline Wildfire Defense conducts comprehensive background checks for all new hires. These checks typically cover the past 7–10 years
and may include employment and education verification
. For roles that require work in the field, driving record verification
is also required. Employment offers are contingent upon the successful completion of these background checks.

About Frontline Wildfire Defense

Founded in 2017 by landscape ecologist and fire mitigation expert Harry Statter, Frontline developed the first fully integrated wildfire defense system to stop the leading cause of home loss in wildfires: ember-driven ignition. The system combines exterior sprinklers, full-coverage design, and connected software for remote monitoring and response, allowing homes to protect themselves long after families evacuate or infrastructure fails.

Proven effective during the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, 96% of homes with Frontline systems survived. That success has earned top industry recognition, including Frontline being recognized as one of TIME’s Best Inventions 2025 in the Green Tech category and receiving the PCBC Gold Nugget Award for “Most Innovative Housing Concept” and the Best of IBS Award for “Best Home Technology.”

As wildfires grow hotter and more frequent, our vision is to give people the tools and strategies to live safely with fire. We’re building a mission-driven team creating real-world solutions in wildfire safety and climate tech.

About This Opportunity

As Frontline's Supply Chain Data Analyst
, you will be the analytical engine behind our procurement and operations function - building the data infrastructure, models, and processes that allow a rapidly scaling hardware company to manage supply effectively. This is a foundational role at a company that just proved its product in one of the most destructive wildfire seasons in California history and is now building the operational backbone to scale nationally.

You'll split your time between hands-on procurement support (approximately 20–30% of your week) and deep data and process improvement work (approximately 70–80%). The procurement side keeps projects moving: managing POs, tracking shipments, and supporting vendor relationships. The analytical side is where you'll have real impact: building models, identifying supply chain inefficiencies, and developing the systems that give leadership the data they need to make decisions at scale.

Key Responsibilities

Procurement Operations Support (20-30% of work week)
Actively support Frontline programs with procurement tasks such as supplier set up, PO creation & approval, price updates, material movement, project tracking, securing of sample & trial materials, tracking and monitoring of shipments, etc.
Internal stakeholder management – establish and support relationships across the numerous functions, commodities and business areas within Frontline
Close out weekly procurement reports for leadership analysis including spend analysis and cost modeling
Work with Project Management to ensure smooth delivery and removal of any materials related to install
Ensure correct departmental coding for all billing reconciliation with finance
Ensure strict compliance to departmental procedures for procurement and escalate to leadership when standards are not met
Proactively escalate any pricing or lead time changes to leadership
Actively develop new vendor relationships to reduce time and cost

Process and Data Improvements (70-80% of work week)
Identify key issues using a variety of data analysis tools and algorithms across a broad range of areas including: operations, logistics, supply and demand planning, inventory optimization, new product readiness, assist in implementing advanced planning systems
Determine root cause of issues, develop solutions, drive change management, manage, monitor supply chain efficiencies, and manage both long and short-term customer delivery plans
Define, analyze, and track key supply chain metrics using data analysis techniques to help assist partnering organizations in making decisions
Create new mathematical models, processes, systems to solve complicated supply chain problems
Translate business requirements into technical/project deliverables

Qualifications:

Must Have:
3–5+ years in supply chain analysis, procurement operations, or a closely related role
Advanced proficiency in Excel - macros, pivot tables, regression analysis, and complex data modeling
Proven ability to build models and reporting tools that are actually used by the business (not just technically sound)
Comfortable working in fast-paced environments with limited historical data and process infrastructure
Strong written and verbal communication skills - you translate data findings into clear recommendations for non-technical stakeholders
Experience managing or supporting procurement operations: PO creation, vendor setup, shipment tracking, billing reconciliation

Nice-to-Have:
Familiarity with ERP or inventory management systems
Background in hardware, manufacturing, or physical goods supply chains - experience with component-level procurement is a strong differentiator
Experience implementing or improving demand planning or inventory optimization systems
Familiarity with project management tools for cross-functional coordination

Compensation & Benefits

Salary Range: $85,000-$115,000 DOE
Company-provided cell phone and laptop
Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance
401(k) retirement plan
Flexible time off + 14 paid holidays (yes, your birthday is one of them!)
Work-from-home stipend to support your remote setup
Remote-first work environment, fostering work-life balance and autonomy
Company-provided equipment
Join a high-performing, mission-driven team doing work that truly matters And much more!

Join Our Mission!

If you're excited about building technology that protects homes and families from wildfire disasters, we want to hear from you! Apply today and become part of a fast-growing team with purpose and innovation at its core.

Diversity and inclusion are essential values at Frontline. We know we'll do our best and most impactful work when we feel represented, and we belong. We encourage talented people from a wide variety of backgrounds and experiences to apply. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

jobs.title: Lead Field Technician
jobs.description:
Position Summary
The Field Technician performs on-site cleaning, flameproofing, and maintenance of commercial drapery, soft goods, and related fabric systems using On-Site's mobile plant units. This is a physically demanding, hands-on role that involves driving a company box truck to client locations, working at height on ladders and lifts to access rigged drapery, and operating specialized cleaning and treatment equipment inside theaters, hotels, schools, hospitals, and performing arts centers. Field Technicians frequently travel out of town for multi-day assignments and are expected to represent On-Site professionally while working independently or as part of a small crew on client premises.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities
•    Drive a company-owned box truck (mobile cleaning unit) to and from client sites, including highway and out-of-town travel, in compliance with all traffic and DOT regulations.
•    Set up and operate the mobile on-site cleaning plant.
•    Access drapery, curtains, and soft goods installed at height using ladders, lifts, or rigging systems; safely take down, clean, treat, and rehang fabric panels.
•    Lift, carry, and maneuver heavy and bulky fabric panels, hardware, and equipment, often in confined backstage, catwalk, or mechanical spaces.
•    Inspect drapery and soft goods for wear, damage, or fire-retardant treatment expiration, and communicate findings to the client and Regional Manager.
•    Perform NFPA 705 field flame testing and document results accurately.
•    Maintain, clean, and perform basic upkeep on the truck, equipment, and cleaning tools between jobs.
•    Follow all site-specific safety protocols (theater, hospital, school, and hotel environments each carry different access and safety rules).
•    Interact professionally with facility staff, building engineers, and client representatives on-site.
•    Complete job documentation, photos, and paperwork required for quality control and client records.
•    Travel out of town for extended periods (multiple days at a time) as job scheduling requires, including overnight stays.

Physical Requirements
•    Ability to regularly lift and carry objects up to 50 lbs, and occasionally up to 75 lbs, with assistance for heavier loads.
•    Ability to climb and work from ladders and lifts at significant heights for extended periods.
•    Comfortable working in catwalks, rigging grids, and other elevated or confined backstage spaces.
•    Ability to stand, kneel, bend, and reach for extended periods during setup, cleaning, and rehang operations.
•    Manual dexterity and stamina to operate cleaning equipment and handle fabric for full work shifts.
•    Ability to safely drive a box truck for extended distances, including multi-hour highway travel.

Travel Requirements
•    Out-of-town travel required, including overnight and multi-day trips depending on client location and job scope.
•    Travel schedule may vary week to week based on the job calendar; some routes are regional, others cross state lines.
•    Company vehicle, fuel, and lodging arrangements provided for qualifying travel per company policy.

Qualifications
•    Valid driver's license in good standing; ability to safely operate a 22-foot box truck (CDL not typically required, but a clean driving record is mandatory).
•    Prior experience in a physically demanding field service, trades, facilities, or installation role preferred (e.g., HVAC, restoration, upholstery, janitorial/facilities, carpet cleaning).
•    Comfortable working at heights on ladders and lifts; prior scaffold, rigging, or ladder-safety training a plus.
•    Strong attention to detail and ability to follow safety and quality procedures without direct daily supervision.
•    Good communication skills for interacting with client site staff.
•    Ability to pass a background check and, where required by client sites (e.g., schools, hospitals), additional screening or badging.

Work Environment
Work is performed primarily on client premises rather than in an office setting, and conditions vary by site — from theater stages and catwalks to hotel ballrooms, school auditoriums, and hospital common areas. Technicians work both independently and as part of a small crew, often coordinating around a facility's own operating hours (e.g., after-hours or overnight access in active hotels or hospitals). The role requires comfort with a changing daily environment, physical exertion, and time away from home during travel assignments.

Salary: $60,000 per year
Benefits:
401(k)
Paid time off

Job Description:

JOB DESCRIPTION

The position description is a guide to the critical duties and essential functions of the job, not an all-inclusive list of responsibilities, qualifications, physical demands, and work environment conditions. Position descriptions are reviewed and revised to meet the changing needs of the organization.

TITLE: Construction Project Coordinator

JOB OVERVIEW: The Construction Project Coordinator provides direct project coordination and support to the construction project management team to ensure successful project development, management, and completion. Responsibilities include assisting with project planning, documentation, scheduling, contractor coordination, management of all furniture procurement, space planning, and departmental move coordination across the organization.

DEPARTMENT: Construction Management Department

WORK HOURS: Typically, Monday - Friday, 7:00 am - 3:30 pm or as necessary to meet departmental needs.

REPORTS TO: Director, Facilities Planning, Design and Construction

Prerequisites:

A high school diploma and minimum of four years of relevant experience in project coordination, construction support, facilities management, or a related field;

OR;

An Associate Degree in a related field and a minimum of two years of relevant experience in project coordination or construction is required.

Experience In Facilities Or Healthcare Construction Is Preferred.

Knowledge of construction project management processes, practices, and tools preferred.

Experience with furniture procurement, space planning, or move coordination preferred.

Proficiency with project management and procurement platforms (e.g., Smartsheet, Bluebeam, or equivalent); CAD experience (AutoCAD or equivalent) preferred for space planning tasks.

Qualifications:

Able to work in a team setting and collaborate effectively with project managers, contractors, vendors, end users, and hospital departments.

Expertise and experience with personal computers and software such as Outlook, Excel, Word, and project management platforms.

Excellent written and verbal communication and customer relations skills in a diverse population.

High attention to detail with ability to manage multiple concurrent workstreams.

Demonstrated ability to use effective judgment in prioritization and time allocation.

Ability to set priorities, produce accurate work, and meet deadlines; ability to function in a setting with a wide variety of duties and numerous interruptions.

Ability to work independently and in teams with good problem solving and organizational skills.

Diligent, results-oriented work habits.

Adept at conducting research into project-related issues, product specifications, and vendor options.

UNIQUE PHYSICAL/MENTAL DEMANDS, ENVIRONMENT AND WORKING CONDITIONS: Regular and punctual attendance is a condition of employment. Physical requirements include having adequate vision and hearing to perform daily responsibilities. Being subject to considerable standing, sitting, stooping, kneeling and exposure to hazardous substances used in the course of work. Requires ability to maintain professional manner when dealing with employees and the public. Requires planning, organizing, and working on multiple tasks at one time. Driving to off-site locations may be required.

Performance Responsibilities:

Generic Job Functions: See Generic Job Description for Administrative Partner.

Essential Responsibilities And Competencies:

Manage all hospital furniture, space planning, moving and relocation needs for all construction projects and standalone requests, including conducting field measurements and site assessments, developing basic furniture layouts using CAD or comparable tools, and coordinating with design consultants when project scope exceeds standard configurations or requires architectural review.

Develop move sequencing plans and phasing schedules in coordination with Project Managers and affected department stakeholders.

Coordinate move logistics with movers, IT, EVS, and facilities staff to ensure seamless execution.

Communicate move plans, timelines, and individual responsibilities to all affected departments; serve as primary point of contact on move day.

Manage all hospital furniture procurement needs, including new construction and renovation projects, department refresh requests, and one-off requests from across the organization.

Coordinate with Project Managers, end users, and design staff to identify furniture requirements and develop specifications aligned with department standards.

Maintain the furniture standards library; escalate non-standard requests requiring design review or management approval.

Liaison with warehouse to monitor inventory of furniture and equipment items that can be repurposed, liaison with ergonomics team on staff furniture needs and proper function.

Oversee and facilitate the installation of equipment and components of projects as assigned by Project Manager.

Assist construction personnel with incoming parts to ensure delivery; direct construction personnel to appropriate people to answer concerns and questions.

Serve as a secondary point of contact for contractors and vendors on assigned projects, routing issues, and decisions to Project Managers as appropriate.

Conduct site visits to observe construction progress, document field conditions, and report status to Project Managers; proactively identify and work to resolve any site issues that may impede project delivery.

Coordinate site access, phasing logistics, and infection control requirements (ICRA/ILSM) with contractors, facilities staff, and affected hospital departments.

Support projects team by coordinating, participating in, and managing project documentation across assigned projects.

Collaborate with internal and external parties to assist with organizing the various components needed to initiate, run, and conclude major projects.

Maintain tracking of action items and follow up with the project management team to ensure timely reply and/or action.

Assist in the development, planning, and execution of meeting agendas and distribute any required materials as needed. Schedule and attend meetings and prepare meeting minutes as required.

Monitor all aspects of project execution to ensure timely contribution by team members, identify potential process bottlenecks, and collaborate with the project management team to resolve issues and maintain project progress.

Serve as a liaison for relevant personnel and department managers when performing project activities.

May perform incidental project management including planning, research, analysis, and implementation of deliverables and action items.

Assist with project closeout procedures including punch list tracking, documentation coordination, and activation planning.

Support Project Managers in preparing stakeholder communications, presentations, and project updates; coordinate with end user departments to gather input, confirm requirements, and communicate project impacts.

Generate purchase requisitions and issue purchase orders in accordance with department procurement and approval procedures.

Manage vendor relationships and coordinate FF&E procurement, delivery, and installation activities, including lead time verification, order tracking, delivery scheduling, and installation oversight to ensure compliance with project requirements and order specifications.

Manage surplus furniture and equipment disposition in connection with moves and project completions.

Maintain FF& E purchase order logs; track and communicate order status to Project Managers and vendors through delivery and installation; process vendor invoices for approval routing and payment in accordance with department procurement procedures.

Reconcile delivered FF&E items against purchase orders; identify and communicate invoice and delivery discrepancies to vendors and Accounts Payable as needed.

Coordinate onboarding of new FF&E vendors with Accounts Payable, ensuring required documentation and account setup are completed prior to order placement.

Assist with broader project budget tracking, invoice review, and change order documentation as directed by Project Managers.

Support Construction Project Administrator position as backup as assigned.

About MediaRadar

MediaRadar, now including the data and capabilities of Vivvix, powers the mission-critical marketing and sales decisions that drive competitive advantage. Our competitive advertising intelligence platform enables clients to achieve peak performance with always-on data and insights that span the media, creative, and business strategies of five million brands across 30+ media channels. By bringing the advertising past, present, and future into focus, our clients rapidly act on the competitive moves and emerging advertising trends impacting their business.

Role Overview

The Data Analyst, Advertising Insights & Strategy is an entry-level role built for someone early in their career who wants to grow into a client-facing analyst. You'll support our custom analytics engagements, including our work for major enterprise accounts, by pulling and organizing enriched competitive advertising data, surfacing creative assets, and building the first pass of analysis that our client-facing analysts use to shape their recommendations. This role is horizontal across the business, meaning you'll support multiple accounts and projects rather than a single client, and it's designed to build the skills needed to grow into a more senior, client-facing analyst role over time.

Requirements

Responsibilities

Data Analysis & Reporting Support (≈60%)

Data Retrieval: Pull enriched competitive advertising datasets (spend, placement, and creative data) from MediaRadar's internal tools for assigned accounts and projects
Share-of-Spend Analysis: Analyze share-of-spend activity across a brand and its competitors to identify which advertisers are gaining or losing ground
Creative Surfacing: Run scripts and use internal tools to surface top-contributing creative assets tied to spend activity, rather than locating them manually
Early Hypothesis Development: Extract metadata and themes from creative and spend data to build an early, data-backed hypothesis (e.g., "advertisers are leaning into rewards messaging this quarter") that senior analysts can validate and build into a client-ready story
Quality Assurance: Check data for anomalies or inconsistencies before handing off analysis to the client-facing analyst team

Cross-Account Support & Growth (≈40%)

Multi-Account Support: Provide analytical support across several accounts and projects rather than a single dedicated client, gaining broad exposure to different verticals and use cases
Frontline Analyst Team Support: Serve as the supporting analyst behind our client-facing team, handling the groundwork so senior analysts can focus on client strategy and delivery
AI-Forward Tooling: Use AI tools, including Claude, as part of your daily workflow to speed up data pulls, first-pass analysis, and reporting — while learning when to rely on it and when to apply your own judgment
Skill Building: Learn MediaRadar's data taxonomy, internal tools, and analytical methodology with the goal of progressing toward a client-facing analyst role
Team Collaboration: Work closely with the analyst and project management team to understand project goals and deliver work on time

Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in Business Analytics, Marketing, Communications, Media, Data Science, or a related field (recent graduates encouraged to apply)
Experience: 0-1 years of professional experience; relevant internships, coursework, or project experience in analytics, marketing, or media are a plus. No prior advertising industry experience required
Technical Curiosity: Comfortable working with data and spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets); interest in or exposure to data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau) is a plus
AI Fluency: Genuine interest in using AI tools like Claude to work more efficiently, paired with the judgment to know when to double-check its output
Communication: Strong writing and organizational skills; able to summarize findings clearly for a technical, internal audience
Aptitude: Detail-oriented, curious, and eager to learn; comfortable managing a few different assignments at once and asking questions when needed

Preferred Skills

Analytical Coursework or Projects: Prior exposure to market research, media, or advertising concepts through coursework, internships, or personal projects
Growth Mindset: Interest in eventually moving into a client-facing analyst or strategy role
Adaptability: Comfortable jumping between different accounts and types of analysis rather than specializing in one vertical right away

Benefits

In addition to career progression, training and development, and an excellent work/life balance, future Radarians can expect a great benefits package that includes:

Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
401k with Company Match
Flexible PTO
Commuter Benefits
Gym Discounts
Summer Fridays

jobs.description:
Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Streamflow Hydrologist
(Hydrogeologist 2) within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires field work. Mondays and Wednesdays are in office days, other days that do not involve field work can be teleworked.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by July 30, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

What You Will Do

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.
Install, operate and maintain water stage height telemetry systems.
Download data loggers and service telemetry systems and/or making upgrades as necessary.
Act as a resource to other agencies and groups that require technical assistance in regards to stream discharge measurement.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education as described below:

Experience
: in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied profession

Experience must include
demonstrated competence in the following skill sets:

Teamwork & Collaboration – Ability to work respectfully and cooperatively with others to support shared goals and maintain productive working relationships.
Adaptability – Ability to adjust to changing field conditions, project demands, and new technologies to remain effective in varied situations.
Critical Thinking & Problem Solving – Ability to interpret information, troubleshoot issues, and make sound decisions to resolve problems and support program objectives.
Field Operations – Ability to plan, prepare for, and conduct fieldwork safely and effectively to collect accurate environmental data.
Hydrologic Measurement & Analysis - Ability to measure stream flow and channel characteristics to develop and update accurate stage-discharge rating curves.
Data Quality & Management – Ability to record, review, and maintain accurate data and notes to ensure data integrity and support scientific analyses. Ability to enter, validate, and analyze data using databases and standard office software to support accurate reporting.
Equipment & Vehicle Operation – Ability to safely operate field equipment, tools, vehicles, and/or boats to access sites and maintain monitoring stations.

Education:
involving a major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

Examples Of How To Qualify

6 years of experience.
5 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
4 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
3 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
2 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
a Master’s degree or higher.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license.

Desired Qualifications

Communication – Ability to clearly share information verbally and in writing to support accurate, effective, and professional interactions.
Workload & Time Management – Ability to plan, organize, and prioritize tasks to meet deadlines and maintain steady workflow.
Professional Conduct – Ability to maintain a calm, respectful, and professional demeanor to support a positive and inclusive work environment.
Project Coordination – Ability to organize field logistics, equipment, and schedules to support efficient and successful project execution.
Scientific Judgment – Ability to interpret environmental data and apply scientific principles to provide objective recommendations.
Hydrologic Monitoring– Ability to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot stream gages and related equipment to collect reliable hydrologic data.
Telemetry & Data Systems – Ability to install, operate, and maintain telemetry and data logger systems to support continuous data collection.
Environmental Sampling – Ability to use scientific instruments and sampling methods to collect water quality or biological data that support environmental assessments.

If you are excited about this role and meet the required qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Chino is an open-pit copper mining complex located 15 miles from the historic mining community of Silver City in southwestern New Mexico. The historic Chino mine was among the world's first low-grade, open-pit copper mines. Today, the operation consists of a 36,000-metric-ton-per-day concentrator that produces copper and a 150-million-pound-per-year solvent extraction/electrowinning plant that produces copper cathode from solution generated by run-of-mine leaching.

Residents and visitors enjoy gentle four seasons, with three hundred days of sunshine a year and low humidity. jobs.description:
Employee Type:
Regular

Job Summary:

Sawtooth Mining is seeking a technically skilled Geologist to join our growing technical team at the Thacker Pass Lithium Clay Surface Mine as we prepare for first ore and transition from a greenfield project to an operating mine. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in one of North America’s most significant lithium projects and contribute directly to the future of critical mineral production.

The successful candidate will be responsible for planning and leading ore-control drilling, as well as collecting, analyzing, and interpreting drilling results for integration into short-range geological, structural, and assay block models. This person will also focus on QA/QC processes and lead the ore control workflow and reconciliation tracking.

Reporting to the Principal Geologist, the Geologist will collaborate closely with mining operations, environmental teams, contractors, and technical personnel across the site.

Work Location: Thacker Pass Project in Orovada, NV.

Job Description:

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

Interpret geologic data and provide geologic structure and assay information and assessments.
Monitor state and federal drilling permit requirements and protection of reserves.
Supervise contractors during geologic drilling and other related projects.
Collect and analyze geotechnical data.
Maintain geologic files, QA/QC data, databases, and samples.
Complete special technical studies as assigned.
Update and maintain the short-range geological, structural, and block models for use in short-range mine planning.
Lead and support Ore Control efforts to ensure that ore is being mined efficiently and reconciliation is tracked correctly.
Perform all duties in accordance with MSHA regulations, state and federal requirements, and company policies.
Promote and maintain a strong safety-first culture.
Support environmental stewardship and regulatory compliance initiatives.

OTHER DUTIES:

Assist with other teams on various mining-related projects.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Some travel will be required.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

Knowledgeable in sedimentary and lithium geology, geochemistry, and hydrology.
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office, Geobank Database software, and Maptek’s Vulcan block modeling software.
Knowledge of Fleet Management System reporting is a plus.
Strong written and interpersonal communication skills are required.
Strong technical writing and presentation skills are required.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate and work in a team environment.
Strong critical thinking skills are required.
Candidate should be based in or willing to relocate to Winnemucca, Nevada (relocation assistance provided).

EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND EXPERIENCE:

At a minimum, a Bachelor’s degree in Geology with 5-10 years of experience in exploration drilling, geological block modeling, and ore control at a surface mining operation.  Preference given to those with a Master’s degree in Geology, Professional Geologist designation, and those currently qualified as a Qualified Person under the SEC’s SK-1300 and Canadian 43-101 regulations.

ANALYSIS OF PHYSICAL DEMANDS OF POSITION:

Intermittently:
None
Occasionally (0 – 1/3 of workday):
Kneeling/crouching (field inspections, troubleshooting); pushing/pulling (light equipment, sampling devices); reaching-above/below shoulder (equipment access, truck cabs); riding in heaving equipment (haul trucks, graders); entering/exiting equipment (3-point contact climbing required); working at elevations/heights (pit walls, elevated platforms); bending/stooping (inspecting ground, samples, equipment); lifting (up to 30-40 pounds: core boxes, tools, sampling gear); carrying (PPE kits, survey gear, laptops); climbing (accessing shovels, highwalls, stairs/ladders); standing (pre-shift meetings, pit observations, mine site walk-throughs).
  Frequently (1/3 – 2/3 of workday):

jobs.title: Field Technician I
jobs.description:
Overview

At UES, we’re a team of more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, geologists, inspectors, technicians, and drillers united by a shared purpose—to make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. As a national leader in geotechnical engineering, environmental consulting, and materials testing and inspection, we collaborate on transformative projects across transportation, energy, water, healthcare, and more. Learn more about the benefits of joining Team UES and our core values at careers.teamues.com.

Position Overview

We are seeking a motivated and hands-on Field Technician I to join our team and support engineering, environmental services, materials testing, and inspection projects. In this role, you will conduct on-site inspections, materials testing, and environmental sampling to ensure construction, infrastructure, and environmental projects meet industry standards and regulatory requirements.

As a Field Technician I, you will work alongside experienced professionals, gaining practical field experience, developing technical skills, and contributing to critical projects that impact communities. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, safety-conscious, and thrives in outdoor work environments, solving challenges in real time and collaborating with a team. This position requires frequent travel to job sites and offers excellent opportunities for growth, technical training, and career advancement in a dynamic industry.

To learn more about the important work our Field Technicians perform, here’s a short video: UES Field Technician

Responsibilities

Conduct field and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, asphalt, aggregate, and other construction materials to verify compliance with project specifications, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
Properly collect, label, and transport samples from job sites to laboratories for further testing and analysis.
Ensure that project testing requirements are met and compliant with project specifications, requirements, and company policies or procedures.
Complete detailed reports, logs, and documentation of test results, ensuring accuracy and timely submission to project managers and stakeholders.
Ensure all testing equipment is properly maintained, and functioning correctly, following company and manufacturer guidelines.
Accurately document test results, observations, and site conditions, preparing and submitting timely and detailed reports, logs, and presentations in accordance with company standards.
Communicate effectively with dispatch, field supervisors, contractors, and project managers, providing real-time updates on job status, site conditions, and any issues encountered.
Adhere to project timelines and schedules, reporting to job sites on time and completing assignments within established deadlines.
Adapt to changing project requirements, schedules, and weather conditions, maintaining flexibility to support business needs.
Participate in ongoing training and certification programs, as required, to maintain technical proficiency and industry compliance.
Follow strict safety protocols and OSHA regulations to maintain a safe work environment, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and adherence to company and client safety guidelines.
Operate and maintain an assigned company vehicle, including scheduling routine maintenance (oil changes, tire checks, fluid levels) and ensuring general cleanliness inside and out.
Perform other duties as assigned to support project goals and company initiatives.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; vocational training or coursework in construction, engineering, geology, or a related field is a plus.
0-3 years of experience in a field-based, outdoor, or physically demanding role preferred (construction, materials testing, geotechnical, or related industry experience is a plus).
Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record; ability to operate company-assigned vehicles safely.
Industry certifications as applicable such as ACI Level 1 Concrete Testing, or ability to obtain within a specified time period.
Commitment to workplace safety, following OSHA standards and company safety policies, including the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Basic computer proficiency, including experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Field Data Collection (FDC) software or similar industry tools.
Mathematical skills sufficient to add, subtract, multiply, and divide into all units of measure using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
Ability to read, write, and interpret blueprints, procedures, manuals, technical documents, and reports related to drilling, safety, and project requirements.
Efficient time management, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to complete tasks efficiently and accurately.
Attention to detail to ensure accurate sample collection, testing procedures, and documentation.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively, demonstrating a strong work ethic and commitment to producing high-quality results.
Flexibility to work varying schedules, including early mornings, weekends, overtime, and potential overnight travel as project demands require.

Travel Requirements

This position requires extensive travel, approximately up to 70% of the time, in support of business

objectives and client engagements. Travel may be both scheduled and on short notice, depending on

project needs. Destinations typically include job sites, field locations, or regional offices, where work may be conducted in outdoor or operational environments. Adherence to all company safety protocols and use of PPE is required during travel and on-site work.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

This position primarily works in an outdoor work environment, regularly exposed to varying field conditions, including:

Sites that may not be accessible by vehicle, requiring travel on foot through wetlands, swamps, grasslands, fields, and other uneven or rugged terrain with natural and man-made obstacles such as sand, brush, and debris.
Moderate to loud noise levels, common in active construction and industrial environments.
Exposure to environmental elements including dirt, dust, sun, heat, humidity, and adverse weather conditions.

The physical requirements for this position may include and are not limited to:

Ability to lift and/or carry 35 to 50 lbs. up to 75 feet, involving regular repetitive motion.
Ability to stand, walk, drive, and operate equipment for extended periods.
Frequent use of hands and arms for typing, handling tools, and operating equipment.
Ability to bend, twist, reach, stoop, pull, kneel, climb, balance, lift, carry, and push as required for fieldwork and inspections.
Ability to speak and hear effectively to communicate in noisy environments and with project teams.
Ability to use your senses to see (including close, distant, and peripheral vision, depth vision, and ability to focus) smell, hear, touch (use hands to reach climb or balance, crouch, stoop, crawl, kneel and sit).

ResourceWise is a leading commodity pricing and market intelligence company specializing in forest products, chemicals, and renewable fuels. With a legacy spanning over 150 years, our mission is to empower clients with the most accurate data, analytics, and strategic insights to drive profitable and sustainable growth. t with expertise in satellite imagery, remote sensing, and geospatial automation to support the development and quality assurance of large-scale land monitoring products. This role combines traditional GIS analysis with AI-driven workflows to improve image interpretation, change detection, and operational efficiency. The ideal candidate has experience working with Sentinel satellite imagery, Python scripting, and geospatial data processing.

Job Duties

Satellite Imagery Quality Assurance
Perform quality assurance (QA/QC) on satellite imagery and derived geospatial products.
Evaluate image quality for cloud cover, atmospheric effects, geometric accuracy, and radiometric consistency.
Identify and document anomalies, processing errors, and data quality issues.
Develop and maintain QA procedures and validation metrics.

Change Detection & Remote Sensing
Design, implement, and refine automated change detection workflows using multi-temporal satellite imagery.
Analyze vegetation and forestry changes using Sentinel imagery.
Validate change detection outputs against reference datasets and ground truth information.
Improve detection accuracy by incorporating new algorithms and best practices.

AI & Process Automation
Identify opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve geospatial production workflows.
Develop AI-assisted routines for image classification, feature extraction, anomaly detection, and quality assurance.
Evaluate emerging AI tools and integrate them into GIS and remote sensing operations.
Collaborate with technical teams to deploy scalable AI-enabled geospatial solutions.

GIS & Programming
Develop Python scripts and geoprocessing tools to automate repetitive GIS tasks.
Process, analyze, and manage large geospatial datasets.
Maintain reproducible workflows using version control and documentation.
Support integration of GIS data into enterprise applications and cloud environments.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in GIS, Geography, Remote Sensing, Environmental Science, Computer Science, or a related field.
3-5 years of professional GIS or remote sensing experience.
Strong experience with Sentinel-1 and/or Sentinel-2 imagery.
Proficiency in Python for geospatial analysis and automation.
Experience with ArcGIS Pro.
Experience performing quality assurance on remote sensing imagery.
Knowledge of raster processing and geospatial data management.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and documentation skills.

Preferred Qualifications include;
Experience with cloud-based geospatial platforms such as Google Earth Engine, AWS, or Azure.
Familiarity with machine learning frameworks such as TensorFlow, PyTorch, or scikit-learn.
Understanding of image classification, segmentation, and computer vision techniques.
Familiarity with SQL and spatial databases (PostGIS, SQL Server Spatial).
Remote Sensing: Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, multispectral imagery
Candidates with experience in forestry, agriculture, environmental monitoring, land cover mapping, natural resource management, or other large-scale Earth observation programs are especially encouraged to apply.

Yearly performance bonus
Medical, dental, and vision benefit programs provided

Education Benefit after 1 year

Under the supervision of the Corporations Program Manager, the incumbent is responsible for performing complex project coordination for the Travis County Corporations. This classification will provide a variety of complex organizational and analytical duties. The role responsibilities include but are not limited to managing one or more projects simultaneously; coordination of planning, scheduling, and analyzing related agreements as well as relevant data. This classification will provide routine analysis of project related information and participate in weekly informational exchanges that are vital for the advancement of projects with internal and external participants. This classification will successfully perform all assigned job responsibilities in support of the Travis County Corporations.

Travis County Corporations is in the Economic Development and Strategic Investments (EDSI) Division of the Planning and & Budget Office and the position report to the Corporations Program Manager. This position works as part of team focused on economic development, strategic planning, investments and affordable housing. This division provides an array of professional services to the County to promote informed decision-making, providing project management and support for county economic development, real estate portfolio management, site redevelopment, and capital planning and investments. The goals of the division are to promote the efficient use of public resources, economic equity and create long-term value for Travis County through collaboration and innovation.

Distinguishing Characteristics

This is a job in the Professional Support job family. This position is distinguished by the amount of organization independence for both actions and decision-making and by the level of supervision, as well as the experience required. This classification will participate in project teams involving various levels of internal and external participants and collaborate to deliver results. This role will develop, maintain, and communicate project documentation, including schedules, milestones, notices, and corresponding budgets. This classification may require a flexible work schedule to meet the needs of the Travis County Corporations.

Duties And Responsibilities

Manages one or more routine projects simultaneously, including planning, scheduling, and coordination during project requirements gathering, development, and implementation stages using established processed and methodologies.
Develops, maintain, and communicate project documentation, including project definition, schedules, notices, and corresponding budgets. Break projects into manageable tasks and set timeframes to meet all related internal, local, state, and federal deadlines. Monitor project progress and troubleshoot complications as necessary.
Works closely with Program Manager and Managing Director to prepare comprehensive action plans, including resources, timeframes, and budget plans. Serve as a point of contact and participate in weekly informational exchanges with internal and external participants.
Participates in continuous review and update to ensure that processes meet changing operational needs. Identify processes for improvement, document existing processes, and identify and analyze gaps between current processes and the desired state.
Ensures completion of projects that are within budget/other resource constraints, meet project deadlines, and deliver quality results by developing contingency plans and quality assurance review of project deliverables.
Tracks, analyzes and documents budget obligations and balances. Use accounting portals for external financial entities to research and examine transactions on project related budgets and inform appropriate stakeholders as necessary.
Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

Education and Experience:

Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Public Administration, Business Administration or a directly related field AND two (2) years of relevant work experience;

OR,

Any combination of education and experience that has been achieved and is equivalent to the stated education and experience and required knowledge, skills, and abilities sufficient to successfully perform the duties and responsibilities of this job.

Licenses, Registrations, Certifications, or Special Requirements:

Valid Texas Driver’s License.

Texas Notary Public.

Applicants are required to attach a resume with the online application.

Preferred:

Certification as a Project Management Professional (PMP) within one (1) year of meeting certification eligibility requirements.

new_jobs.title: Sr. Data Analyst
new_jobs.description:
Company Description:

Sagetap is a rapidly growing startup changing how enterprise technology executives discover and evaluate software. Our AI-driven platform anonymously connects tech buyers with the industry’s most credible technology vendors, helping them cut through the noise and solve their biggest problems.

Backed by investors like NFX Ventures, Uncorrelated Ventures, and Emergent Ventures, we are on a mission to fundamentally change software discovery for senior technology leaders, fostering meaningful connections in a non-sales setting.

We’re a tight-knit, fast-moving team that values curiosity, transparency, and impact. If you’re energetic, results-oriented, and excited to work in an early-stage environment, come help us shape the future of technology buying at Sagetap!
Job Description

As a Senior Data Analyst at Sagetap, you'll serve as the strategic analytics partner to Product, Growth, Engineering, Design, and Leadership. You'll use data to shape product strategy, influence roadmap decisions, and identify the highest-impact opportunities for marketplace growth.

You'll own the product analytics function; from defining KPIs and experimentation frameworks to building trusted reporting and scalable datasets. Your work will help leadership understand what is happening in the business, why it is happening, and what we should do next.

What you will do:

Serve as the strategic analytics partner to Product, Growth, Engineering, and Design, helping prioritize roadmap investments through quantitative analysis and marketplace insights.
Support growth by generating insights and reports from Sagetap proprietary data.
Own the measurement framework for product initiatives by defining KPIs, evaluating feature performance, identifying root causes behind metric movement, and presenting recommendations to leadership.
Lead experimentation strategy by designing, evaluating, and scaling A/B tests and product experiments.
Build executive-ready dashboards, analyses, and self-service reporting that improve decision making across Product, GTM, and Leadership.
Create and maintain scalable analytics datasets using DBT and modern data modeling best practices.
Manage Database Categorization of our technology categories and vendors.
Partner with executive leadership to answer strategic business questions and influence company priorities through data.
Support growth by generating insights and reports from Sagetap proprietary data. 
Research cybersecurity and AI markets to identify trends that inform product strategy.
Leverage LLMs to improve internal workflows and enrich Sagetap's product database.

Qualifications:

5+ years of experience in Product Analytics, Data Analytics, Growth Analytics, or Data Science, preferably in B2B SaaS, marketplaces, or product-led growth companies.
Expert SQL and Python proficiency.
Hands-on experience with DBT, Mixpanel, Omni (or similar BI tools), Git, experimentation frameworks, and modern data warehouses.
Experience defining KPIs and measurement strategies for product organizations.

About Frontline Wildfire Defense

Founded in 2017 by landscape ecologist and fire mitigation expert Harry Statter, Frontline developed the first fully integrated wildfire defense system to stop the leading cause of home loss in wildfires: ember-driven ignition. The system combines exterior sprinklers, full-coverage design, and connected software for remote monitoring and response, allowing homes to protect themselves long after families evacuate or infrastructure fails.

Proven effective during the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires, 96% of homes with Frontline systems survived. That success has earned top industry recognition, including Frontline being recognized as one of TIME’s Best Inventions 2025 in the Green Tech category and receiving the PCBC Gold Nugget Award for “Most Innovative Housing Concept” and the Best of IBS Award for “Best Home Technology.”

As wildfires grow hotter and more frequent, our vision is to give people the tools and strategies to live safely with fire. We’re building a mission-driven team creating real-world solutions in wildfire safety and climate tech.

As Frontline's Supply Chain Data Analyst

new_jobs.title: Lead Field Technician
new_jobs.description:
Position Summary
The Field Technician performs on-site cleaning, flameproofing, and maintenance of commercial drapery, soft goods, and related fabric systems using On-Site's mobile plant units. This is a physically demanding, hands-on role that involves driving a company box truck to client locations, working at height on ladders and lifts to access rigged drapery, and operating specialized cleaning and treatment equipment inside theaters, hotels, schools, hospitals, and performing arts centers. Field Technicians frequently travel out of town for multi-day assignments and are expected to represent On-Site professionally while working independently or as part of a small crew on client premises.
Essential Duties & Responsibilities
•    Drive a company-owned box truck (mobile cleaning unit) to and from client sites, including highway and out-of-town travel, in compliance with all traffic and DOT regulations.
•    Set up and operate the mobile on-site cleaning plant.
•    Access drapery, curtains, and soft goods installed at height using ladders, lifts, or rigging systems; safely take down, clean, treat, and rehang fabric panels.
•    Lift, carry, and maneuver heavy and bulky fabric panels, hardware, and equipment, often in confined backstage, catwalk, or mechanical spaces.
•    Inspect drapery and soft goods for wear, damage, or fire-retardant treatment expiration, and communicate findings to the client and Regional Manager.
•    Perform NFPA 705 field flame testing and document results accurately.
•    Maintain, clean, and perform basic upkeep on the truck, equipment, and cleaning tools between jobs.
•    Follow all site-specific safety protocols (theater, hospital, school, and hotel environments each carry different access and safety rules).
•    Interact professionally with facility staff, building engineers, and client representatives on-site.
•    Complete job documentation, photos, and paperwork required for quality control and client records.
•    Travel out of town for extended periods (multiple days at a time) as job scheduling requires, including overnight stays.

Physical Requirements
•    Ability to regularly lift and carry objects up to 50 lbs, and occasionally up to 75 lbs, with assistance for heavier loads.
•    Ability to climb and work from ladders and lifts at significant heights for extended periods.
•    Comfortable working in catwalks, rigging grids, and other elevated or confined backstage spaces.
•    Ability to stand, kneel, bend, and reach for extended periods during setup, cleaning, and rehang operations.
•    Manual dexterity and stamina to operate cleaning equipment and handle fabric for full work shifts.
•    Ability to safely drive a box truck for extended distances, including multi-hour highway travel.

Travel Requirements
•    Out-of-town travel required, including overnight and multi-day trips depending on client location and job scope.
•    Travel schedule may vary week to week based on the job calendar; some routes are regional, others cross state lines.
•    Company vehicle, fuel, and lodging arrangements provided for qualifying travel per company policy.

Qualifications
•    Valid driver's license in good standing; ability to safely operate a 22-foot box truck (CDL not typically required, but a clean driving record is mandatory).
•    Prior experience in a physically demanding field service, trades, facilities, or installation role preferred (e.g., HVAC, restoration, upholstery, janitorial/facilities, carpet cleaning).
•    Comfortable working at heights on ladders and lifts; prior scaffold, rigging, or ladder-safety training a plus.
•    Strong attention to detail and ability to follow safety and quality procedures without direct daily supervision.
•    Good communication skills for interacting with client site staff.
•    Ability to pass a background check and, where required by client sites (e.g., schools, hospitals), additional screening or badging.

Work Environment
Work is performed primarily on client premises rather than in an office setting, and conditions vary by site — from theater stages and catwalks to hotel ballrooms, school auditoriums, and hospital common areas. Technicians work both independently and as part of a small crew, often coordinating around a facility's own operating hours (e.g., after-hours or overnight access in active hotels or hospitals). The role requires comfort with a changing daily environment, physical exertion, and time away from home during travel assignments.

Salary: $60,000 per year
Benefits:
401(k)
Paid time off

This is a remote, temporary position working approximately 30 hours per week.

Temporary positions at the University of Colorado are not benefits-eligible, however, all positions are eligible for paid sick leave .

About MediaRadar

MediaRadar, now including the data and capabilities of Vivvix, powers the mission-critical marketing and sales decisions that drive competitive advantage. By bringing the advertising past, present, and future into focus, our clients rapidly act on the competitive moves and emerging advertising trends impacting their business.

Role Overview

The Data Analyst, Advertising Insights & Strategy is an entry-level role built for someone early in their career who wants to grow into a client-facing analyst. You'll support our custom analytics engagements, including our work for major enterprise accounts, by pulling and organizing enriched competitive advertising data, surfacing creative assets, and building the first pass of analysis that our client-facing analysts use to shape their recommendations. This role is horizontal across the business, meaning you'll support multiple accounts and projects rather than a single client, and it's designed to build the skills needed to grow into a more senior, client-facing analyst role over time.

Requirements

Responsibilities

Data Analysis & Reporting Support (≈60%)

Data Retrieval: Pull enriched competitive advertising datasets (spend, placement, and creative data) from MediaRadar's internal tools for assigned accounts and projects
Share-of-Spend Analysis: Analyze share-of-spend activity across a brand and its competitors to identify which advertisers are gaining or losing ground
Creative Surfacing: Run scripts and use internal tools to surface top-contributing creative assets tied to spend activity, rather than locating them manually
Early Hypothesis Development: Extract metadata and themes from creative and spend data to build an early, data-backed hypothesis (e.g., "advertisers are leaning into rewards messaging this quarter") that senior analysts can validate and build into a client-ready story
Quality Assurance: Check data for anomalies or inconsistencies before handing off analysis to the client-facing analyst team

Cross-Account Support & Growth (≈40%)

Multi-Account Support: Provide analytical support across several accounts and projects rather than a single dedicated client, gaining broad exposure to different verticals and use cases
Frontline Analyst Team Support: Serve as the supporting analyst behind our client-facing team, handling the groundwork so senior analysts can focus on client strategy and delivery
AI-Forward Tooling: Use AI tools, including Claude, as part of your daily workflow to speed up data pulls, first-pass analysis, and reporting — while learning when to rely on it and when to apply your own judgment
Skill Building: Learn MediaRadar's data taxonomy, internal tools, and analytical methodology with the goal of progressing toward a client-facing analyst role
Team Collaboration: Work closely with the analyst and project management team to understand project goals and deliver work on time

Qualifications

Education: Bachelor's degree in Business Analytics, Marketing, Communications, Media, Data Science, or a related field (recent graduates encouraged to apply)
Experience: 0-1 years of professional experience; relevant internships, coursework, or project experience in analytics, marketing, or media are a plus. No prior advertising industry experience required
Technical Curiosity: Comfortable working with data and spreadsheets (Excel/Google Sheets); interest in or exposure to data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau) is a plus
AI Fluency: Genuine interest in using AI tools like Claude to work more efficiently, paired with the judgment to know when to double-check its output
Communication: Strong writing and organizational skills; able to summarize findings clearly for a technical, internal audience
Aptitude: Detail-oriented, curious, and eager to learn; comfortable managing a few different assignments at once and asking questions when needed

Preferred Skills

Analytical Coursework or Projects: Prior exposure to market research, media, or advertising concepts through coursework, internships, or personal projects
Growth Mindset: Interest in eventually moving into a client-facing analyst or strategy role
Adaptability: Comfortable jumping between different accounts and types of analysis rather than specializing in one vertical right away

Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
401k with Company Match
Flexible PTO
Commuter Benefits
Gym Discounts

Description

Keeping Washington Clean and Evergreen

The Department of Ecology is hiring a Streamflow Hydrologist
(Hydrogeologist 2) within the Environmental Assessment Program .

Location:

Central Region Office in Union Gap, WA .
Upon hire, you must live within a commutable distance from the duty station.

Schedule

This position is eligible for telework and flexible schedule options.
This position requires field work. Mondays and Wednesdays are in office days, other days that do not involve field work can be teleworked.
Schedules are dependent upon position needs and are subject to change.

Application Timeline

Apply by July 30, 2026
Applications submitted after the date above may not be reviewed unless additional qualified applicants are needed.

Duties

In this role, you will collect and process credible stream hydrology information for river systems or basins that are reliable, accurate and timely. You will possess and demonstrate the skills required to install and operate stream gages in the assigned geographical area. You will also evaluate and develop rating curves, reviewing data for completeness and overall quality and providing field support to keep stations on-line and reporting accurate information.

What You Will Do

Using sound scientific principles, select measurement points that are representative of the measurement of stream discharge.
Develop individual state discharge rating curves for each measurement site by taking flow measurements that define this relationship over the entire flow regime.
Carry out cross section measurements at individual measurement sites so that accurate calculations can confirm the stage discharge rating curves developed.
Track the change in channel cross-section over time and adjust the stage-discharge rating table.
Install, operate and maintain water stage height telemetry systems.
Download data loggers and service telemetry systems and/or making upgrades as necessary.
Act as a resource to other agencies and groups that require technical assistance in regards to stream discharge measurement.

Qualifications

For detailed information on how we calculate experience and responses to other frequently asked questions, please visit our Recruitment website .

Required Qualifications

Six years of experience and/or education as described below:

Experience
: in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied profession

Experience must include
demonstrated competence in the following skill sets:

Teamwork & Collaboration – Ability to work respectfully and cooperatively with others to support shared goals and maintain productive working relationships.
Adaptability – Ability to adjust to changing field conditions, project demands, and new technologies to remain effective in varied situations.
Critical Thinking & Problem Solving – Ability to interpret information, troubleshoot issues, and make sound decisions to resolve problems and support program objectives.
Field Operations – Ability to plan, prepare for, and conduct fieldwork safely and effectively to collect accurate environmental data.
Hydrologic Measurement & Analysis - Ability to measure stream flow and channel characteristics to develop and update accurate stage-discharge rating curves.
Data Quality & Management – Ability to record, review, and maintain accurate data and notes to ensure data integrity and support scientific analyses. Ability to enter, validate, and analyze data using databases and standard office software to support accurate reporting.
Equipment & Vehicle Operation – Ability to safely operate field equipment, tools, vehicles, and/or boats to access sites and maintain monitoring stations.

Education:
involving a major study in hydrogeology, hydrology, geology or closely allied field.

Examples Of How To Qualify

6 years of experience.
5 years of experience AND 30-59 semester or 45-89 quarter college credits.
4 years of experience AND 60-89 semester or 90-134 quarter college credits (Associate’s degree).
3 years of experience AND 90-119 semester or 135-179 quarter college credits.
2 years of experience AND a Bachelor’s degree.
a Master’s degree or higher.

Special Requirements/Conditions Of Employment

Must possess and maintain a valid driver's license.

Desired Qualifications

Communication – Ability to clearly share information verbally and in writing to support accurate, effective, and professional interactions.
Workload & Time Management – Ability to plan, organize, and prioritize tasks to meet deadlines and maintain steady workflow.
Professional Conduct – Ability to maintain a calm, respectful, and professional demeanor to support a positive and inclusive work environment.
Project Coordination – Ability to organize field logistics, equipment, and schedules to support efficient and successful project execution.
Scientific Judgment – Ability to interpret environmental data and apply scientific principles to provide objective recommendations.
Hydrologic Monitoring– Ability to operate, maintain, and troubleshoot stream gages and related equipment to collect reliable hydrologic data.
Telemetry & Data Systems – Ability to install, operate, and maintain telemetry and data logger systems to support continuous data collection.
Environmental Sampling – Ability to use scientific instruments and sampling methods to collect water quality or biological data that support environmental assessments.

Job Summary:

Sawtooth Mining is seeking a technically skilled Geologist to join our growing technical team at the Thacker Pass Lithium Clay Surface Mine as we prepare for first ore and transition from a greenfield project to an operating mine. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in one of North America’s most significant lithium projects and contribute directly to the future of critical mineral production.

The successful candidate will be responsible for planning and leading ore-control drilling, as well as collecting, analyzing, and interpreting drilling results for integration into short-range geological, structural, and assay block models. This person will also focus on QA/QC processes and lead the ore control workflow and reconciliation tracking.

Reporting to the Principal Geologist, the Geologist will collaborate closely with mining operations, environmental teams, contractors, and technical personnel across the site.

Work Location: Thacker Pass Project in Orovada, NV.

Job Description:

ESSENTIAL DUTIES:

Interpret geologic data and provide geologic structure and assay information and assessments.
Monitor state and federal drilling permit requirements and protection of reserves.
Supervise contractors during geologic drilling and other related projects.
Collect and analyze geotechnical data.
Maintain geologic files, QA/QC data, databases, and samples.
Complete special technical studies as assigned.
Update and maintain the short-range geological, structural, and block models for use in short-range mine planning.
Lead and support Ore Control efforts to ensure that ore is being mined efficiently and reconciliation is tracked correctly.
Perform all duties in accordance with MSHA regulations, state and federal requirements, and company policies.
Promote and maintain a strong safety-first culture.
Support environmental stewardship and regulatory compliance initiatives.

OTHER DUTIES:

Assist with other teams on various mining-related projects.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Some travel will be required.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

Knowledgeable in sedimentary and lithium geology, geochemistry, and hydrology.
Advanced knowledge of Microsoft Office, Geobank Database software, and Maptek’s Vulcan block modeling software.
Knowledge of Fleet Management System reporting is a plus.
Strong written and interpersonal communication skills are required.
Strong technical writing and presentation skills are required.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate and work in a team environment.
Strong critical thinking skills are required.
Candidate should be based in or willing to relocate to Winnemucca, Nevada (relocation assistance provided).

EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND EXPERIENCE:

At a minimum, a Bachelor’s degree in Geology with 5-10 years of experience in exploration drilling, geological block modeling, and ore control at a surface mining operation.  Preference given to those with a Master’s degree in Geology, Professional Geologist designation, and those currently qualified as a Qualified Person under the SEC’s SK-1300 and Canadian 43-101 regulations.

ANALYSIS OF PHYSICAL DEMANDS OF POSITION:

Intermittently:
None
Occasionally (0 – 1/3 of workday):
Kneeling/crouching (field inspections, troubleshooting); pushing/pulling (light equipment, sampling devices); reaching-above/below shoulder (equipment access, truck cabs); riding in heaving equipment (haul trucks, graders); entering/exiting equipment (3-point contact climbing required); working at elevations/heights (pit walls, elevated platforms); bending/stooping (inspecting ground, samples, equipment); lifting (up to 30-40 pounds: core boxes, tools, sampling gear); carrying (PPE kits, survey gear, laptops); climbing (accessing shovels, highwalls, stairs/ladders); standing (pre-shift meetings, pit observations, mine site walk-throughs).
  Frequently (1/3 – 2/3 of workday):
Navigation of active mining areas (around haul trucks); walking (pit floors, waste dumps, uneven and rocky terrain); walking on uneven ground (loose ore, benches, slopes); driving light vehicles (long distances across mine site (minimum of 10 miles/day); sitting (engineering design, scheduling, reporting, AutoCAD, Vulcan, Microsoft Office Applications).
Constantly (2/3 – 3/3 of workday):
Fine motor skills-typing, instruments (engineering software, GPS/survey tools); vision (hazard recognition, surveying, reading plans/screens); hearing (radio communication, alarms, heavy equipment); communication (coordination with operators, supervisors, contractors); depth perception (working near edges, haul roads, highwalls); situational awareness (MSHA safety environment).
